items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I became acquainted with some of the musicians of Fess Williams' orchestra... except George Temple whom I talked with and told him that I had seen him before.

ctx.x: There were two band stands and one of the bands that were playing when I came in was the Fess Williams Orchestra which I had heard about. Fess was dressed in a tuxedo with rhinestones in the lapels and a top hat with the same kind of stones around the band of the hat. The other musicians were dressed in regular tuxedos. I recognised having seen one of the trumpet players when I was younger and had to put/long pants to get into the

Theatres up town in Cincy. I did not know his name but the face I remembered so I asked Cecil who he was and he told me that it was George Temple. George and his brother had been in Cooper's Black and White Show which was a mixed show that I had seen in Cincinnati when I was about 16 years old.

The rest of Fess Williams Orchestra was another trumpet, trombone, 3 saxes and a full rhythm section, piano, banjo, tuba and drums. But I did not hear anything from this orchestra that was sensational or excited my emotional feelings and in fact it was a corny band as far as I was concerned, which did not merit the praise that I had heard.
